newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs flat-off $0.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs flat-off $0.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were mostly steady, with instances $0.50 per cwt lower, livestock dealers said.

Prices were mostly steady as light marketings offset lighter demand going into the weekend, they said. The exception was Indiana where extremely light buying interest pulled prices lower, the dealers said.
Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $57.00 to $58.00 in the country and $58.00 to $59.50 at plants.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $57.00-$58.00 in the country and $58.50-$59.50 at plants.

Illinois hogs sold steady to $58.00 to $58.50 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants, dealers there said. Prices in Illinois could firm if marketings do not pick up later in the morning, one Illinois dealer said.
"Runs are light and demand is just firm enough that if we don't get a few more hogs, this market could gain a little strength," he said.
Ohio hogs sold steady, with a top at $58.00 in the country and $60.50 at plants.
Hog slaughter Saturday was seen light, with estimates from 22,000 to 25,000 head versus 23,000 a week ago and 11,000 a year ago.
